title: test-0005-MAT-BASICGEOM
passage: Rohan visits a local craft market to buy materials for his geometry project. He sees a beautiful hand-painted sign shaped like a triangle, but it is tilted sideways with its apex pointing to the left. The shopkeeper explains that a triangle is simply a closed figure with three line segments, regardless of its orientation. Rohan then looks at a circular plate. The shopkeeper draws a line segment from one edge of the plate to the other, passing exactly through the center point, and calls it the diameter. He notes that any line segment connecting two points on the circle must pass through the center to be called a diameter. Next, Rohan examines a decorative wire sculpture. It is a closed curve made of straight lines that cross over each other in the middle. The shopkeeper clarifies that even if a curve crosses itself, it remains a curve. Finally, Rohan buys a ruler to measure a line segment. He notices that the segment from point A to point B is exactly the same length as the segment from point B to point A, proving that the order of naming endpoints does not change the segment itself.
summary: The shopkeeper draws a line from one edge of the plate to the other, passing through the center point, and calls it the diameter. He says that any line segment connecting two points on a circle must go through the center to be called a diameter.
